question: What freshwater fish evidence does the public AWTIP Tunnel 4 monitoring report provide for Ipo Lake, Angat River, Bigte Creek, and Sta Maria River, and can it be kept distinct from the unresolved Tunnel 5 2016 comparison source?

source.citation: Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System. (2019). Environmental Monitoring Report, Semi-Annual Report January–June 2019: Philippines—Angat Water Transmission Improvement Project, Design and Construction of Ipo to Bigte Tunnel No. 4. Prepared for the Asian Development Bank. Appendix 8.7: Freshwater Ecology Monitoring Report (Dry & Wet Season 2018), by Roberto C. Pagulayan, PhD (version 1, January 2019).
source.accessNote: The public ADB-hosted borrower report PDF was retrieved and its freshwater appendix was reviewed as text and page images. A temporary working copy was used for this review but was not added to the repository. ADB states that this is a borrower document and its views do not necessarily represent ADB.

studyScope.projectContext: Freshwater ecology monitoring for the AWTIP Tunnel 4 project, covering the Ipo Dam intake area and the Bigte tunnel-end area. The report describes these as project-impact study areas; that context does not imply public fishing access.
studyScope.seasonalScope: The report identifies dry-season sampling in May 2018 and wet-season sampling in September 2018. Table 1 assigns station dates individually; one dry-season station date and some wet-season dates differ from the main-report summary and are retained as printed below.

biotaSamplingStations.localityAsReported: Ipo Lake upstream, about 100 m from the Angat spillway
Ipo Lake midstream, near the Bantay Gubat campsite
Angat River, about 200 m downstream from Ipo Dam structure
Angat River, vicinity of Bitbit Bridge
Angat River at Barangay Pogpog, Norzagaray; about 1 km upstream of the August 2013 EIA sampling site
biotaSamplingStations.seasonalNote: Additional wet-season station; no dry-season date is listed.

biotaSamplingStations.localityAsReported: Bigte Creek tributary along the Manila Water compound (biota site)
Bigte Creek tributary within Salonga property, about 20 m from the SWB2A water-sampling site
Sta Maria River just after San Jose Bridge
biotaSamplingStations.dateNote: The May date in Table 1 predates the main report's stated May 28–30 dry-season survey window; not silently corrected.

studyScope.coordinateRoleAndLimits: Coordinates above are source-reported biota sampling-station coordinates, not fish-specific capture coordinates, GPS tracks, fishing spots, waterbody boundaries, or legal access points. The report does not state coordinate uncertainty. Water-quality station coordinates were not substituted for the biota stations.
studyScope.samplingDatesNote: The main report says the dry-season survey ran May 28–30 and the wet-season survey was conducted September 20, 2018, while Table 1 lists Site 8 on May 23 and Sites 5b–8 on September 21. Station-level dates are transcribed as printed; these discrepancies need source-owner clarification before any event-level date projection.

methodsAndTaxonEvidence.methodAsReported: At riverine sites, fish were collected with electrofishing gear. At Ipo Dam lake sites, the team used seine nets with 1 cm and 1 mm mesh; a mosquito net was also used for smaller fish in wadable areas. The report describes 50 m stream reaches and a 10 m radius in mid-lake sampling areas. Samples were preliminarily sorted, identified, and preserved on ice.
methodsAndTaxonEvidence.reportedTaxonCountMeaning: The narrative says 19 fish species were collected across the sites; Table 13 displays 19 numbered scientific-name rows and seasonal site columns. The table labels its values as density per 100 square metres. This review records the names as source-reported; it does not convert density cells into occurrence records or recalculate abundance.
methodsAndTaxonEvidence.taxonomyDisposition: No accepted-name normalization or specimen re-identification was performed. Preserve table spelling in this evidence artifact; resolve names against a current taxonomic authority and, if possible, vouchers before any species assertion.

sourceNameVariants.location: Table 13 versus photo caption; retain both pending taxonomic review

methodsAndTaxonEvidence.specimenTraceability: The appendix says samples were identified and preserved on ice, but the reviewed report gives no museum catalogue numbers, voucher accession identifiers, or retained specimen repository for these fish.

sourceConsistencyAndRelationships.baselineCountConflict: The appendix first says 19 fish species were three more than the August 2013 and May 2014 samples, then later says 19 was two more. Do not reuse either difference as a verified comparison statistic.

comparisonWithTunnel5Eprmp.assessment: This is a distinct Tunnel 4 monitoring report for 2018, with its own 19-row fish table and 2013/2014 baseline comparison. The Tunnel 5 EPRMP separately compares a reported 2016 survey and a 2022 survey. No shared sampling dates, station list, specimen IDs, or source citation establish that this 2018 Tunnel 4 table is the EPRMP's 2016 survey or resolves the EPRMP's 17-claim/15-visible-row discrepancy.
comparisonWithTunnel5Eprmp.disposition: Maintain both sources separately; keep the identity and source lineage of the EPRMP's 2016 comparison unresolved.

sourceConsistencyAndRelationships.dietDisposition: No local stomach-content or feeding study was reviewed in this appendix. General ecology text is not treated as local diet evidence, natural prey guidance, or bait advice.
sourceConsistencyAndRelationships.imageDisposition: Fish photographs appear in the appendix, but no image-to-taxon or item-level reuse review was performed for them. No source photograph, figure, or map was copied into this artifact or the app.

rightsAndPublication.decision: The report is a borrower document hosted by ADB. No item-specific open license or permission to redistribute its fish table, photographs, maps, or derived rows was verified. Use this attributed transcription only as internal research evidence pending rights review; do not project it to the app or redistribute media.
rightsAndPublication.rawRetention: A temporary PDF copy was hashed for review and was not committed or retained in the repository.

nextActions: Run the 19 source-reported names through the existing taxonomic cross-check workflow, preserving unresolved spellings and provenance.
Review the table's species-by-site density cells as a separate transcription task before considering any station-level association; do not treat an empty cell as proof of absence.
Keep the Tunnel 5 EPRMP's 2016 comparison source unresolved until a source explicitly ties it to dated stations or identifiable specimens.
Continue independent freshwater source review for other Central Luzon basins; this single historical project survey does not complete Bulacan or Region III.

sources.supports: Public borrower EMR and Appendix 8.7: survey context, dates, sampling stations and coordinates, collection methods, 19 source-reported fish taxa, Table 13, and internal count/name variants.
Separate Tunnel 5 EPRMP comparison claim; not evidence that the 2018 Tunnel 4 survey is its underlying 2016 source.
